passages.title: Libraries in the Age of Screens
passages.text: Every few years, a prediction is made that public libraries will soon disappear. Books, it is argued, are available on phones, and information is only a click away. Yet the footfall in many town libraries suggests otherwise. A library today is not merely a store of books; it is a quiet, free and welcoming space where a student without a table at home can prepare for an examination, where a retired teacher can read the newspapers, and where a child can discover that stories are not confined to a screen. Critics point to the cost of maintaining buildings and staff. But what is the price of a reading habit? Municipal bodies that starve libraries of funds save little and lose much. The need of the hour is not closure but modernisation: more digital catalogues, longer opening hours and books in local languages. A society that stops investing in its libraries should not be surprised when it finds its imagination running short.

passages.title: The Old Well
passages.text:
The old well at the edge of our village
Has watched three generations come and go;
Its stones are green with moss and memory,
Its water cool as the evening's first breeze.
The women came at dawn with brass pots shining,
Laughing, they filled them, sharing news and sorrow;
Children dropped pebbles, listening for the splash,
Counting the seconds till the echo rose.
Now a tap stands silent in each courtyard,
And no one walks the winding path to the well.
The rope is frayed, the pulley rusts and sleeps,
But nothing in the dark has quite forgotten.
Yet at night, when the moon leans over its rim,
The well still holds a sky no one comes to drink.

passages.title: Nitrogen and the Root Nodules
passages.text: Plants need nitrogen to build proteins, yet the air around them is nearly four-fifths nitrogen. The difficulty is that atmospheric nitrogen exists as two atoms joined by a very strong bond, and most plants cannot break it. Certain bacteria, such as Rhizobium, can. They live in small swellings called nodules on the roots of pulses like gram and pea, and convert nitrogen from the air into compounds that the plant can absorb. In return, the plant supplies the bacteria with sugars made in its leaves. This partnership is an example of symbiosis, in which both organisms benefit. Farmers have long known that growing a pulse crop in rotation with cereals improves the soil, though they did not always know the reason. Today, this knowledge helps reduce the use of chemical fertilisers, which are costly and can pollute water when rain washes them from the fields.

questions.question: She said to me, 'Where do you live?' The correct indirect speech is:
options: She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where I lived.
She told me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order becomes that of a statement (subject before verb), 'said to' becomes 'asked', and the present tense shifts to the past. Option 1 does this; options 0 and 3 keep question word order; option 2 uses 'told', which is wrong for a question.

questions.question: Identify the cleft sentence from the options below.
options: The window was broken by Ravi.
It was Ravi who broke the window.
Ravi, who broke the window, ran away.
questions.explanation: A cleft sentence splits one clause into two parts to give focus, using 'It is/was ... that/who'. Option 2 focuses on Ravi. Option 0 is a simple active sentence, option 1 is passive, and option 3 has a non-defining relative clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Not only ___ the exam, but he also won a scholarship.
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with a negative adverbial such as 'Not only', the auxiliary comes before the subject: 'did he pass'. The other options keep normal word order or omit the auxiliary.

questions.question: If water is heated to 100°C at sea level, it ___.
questions.explanation: The zero conditional (if + present simple, present simple) states a general scientific truth, so 'boils' is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is an elliptical construction (some words are omitted but understood)?
options: She wanted to go, but she could not go.
I was tired and I was hungry.
He is as tall as his brother is tall.
questions.explanation: 'Though tired' stands for 'Though he was tired', so the subject and verb are omitted. The other sentences express every element in full.

questions.question: I need ___ information about the admission process.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun, so it takes 'some'. 'Many', 'a few' and 'several' are used only with plural countable nouns.

questions.question: You ___ smoke in this area; it is strictly prohibited.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition. 'Needn't' means no necessity, 'may' gives permission, and 'ought' must be followed by 'to'.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: I am late, ___?
questions.explanation: The standard tag for 'I am' is 'aren't I'. 'Amn't I' is not used in standard English.

questions.question: The phrasal verb 'put off' in 'The meeting was put off till Monday' means:
questions.explanation: 'Put off' means to postpone. 'Put out' means to extinguish, 'put on' means to wear, and 'put up with' means to tolerate.

questions.question: Bread and butter ___ my favourite breakfast.
questions.explanation: When two nouns form one single idea, the verb is singular: 'Bread and butter is'.

questions.question: By the time we reached the cinema, the film ___.
questions.explanation: Two past actions: the earlier one takes the past perfect ('had started'), the later one the simple past ('reached'). The other forms do not show the earlier action.

questions.question: Identify the sentence containing a non-defining relative clause.
options: The boy who is standing there is my cousin.
My uncle, who lives in Durg, is a doctor.
This is the house that Jack built.
questions.explanation: A non-defining clause adds extra information and is set off by commas, as in 'who lives in Durg'. Options 0 and 2 are defining clauses (no commas), and option 3 has a noun clause.

questions.question: Rewrite as a simple sentence: 'The tea was so hot that we could not drink it.'
options: The tea was too hot for us to drink.
The tea was very hot to drink.
The tea was enough hot to drink.
The tea was so hot to drink.
questions.explanation: 'So ... that ... could not' is converted to 'too ... to'. The other options are ungrammatical or change the meaning.

questions.question: In the sentence 'I will wait here until you return', the clause 'until you return' is a/an ___ clause.
questions.explanation: The clause tells when the waiting will continue, so it is an adverb clause of time modifying the verb 'wait'. It does not name a thing (noun), describe a noun (adjective) or join equal clauses (coordinate).

questions.question: In 'Tired of waiting, she left', the words 'Tired of waiting' form a:
questions.explanation: 'Tired' is a past participle used adjectivally, so the group is a participial (non-finite) phrase modifying 'she'. It has no finite verb, it does not act as a noun (gerund), and it has no 'to + verb'.

questions.question: In which of these sentences does 'bank' mean 'the sloping land beside a river'?
options: I deposited money in the bank.
We sat on the bank and watched the boats.
The bank will close at four.
questions.explanation: Only option 2 refers to the land beside water. In the others 'bank' means a financial institution or a store of blood.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: She could not ___ the loud noise any longer.
questions.explanation: 'Bear' means to tolerate. 'Bare' means uncovered, 'beer' is a drink and 'bier' is a stand for a coffin.

questions.question: Choose the correct collocation: He ___ a serious mistake in the calculation.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'make a mistake'. 'Do', 'take' and 'give' do not collocate with 'mistake'.

questions.question: Choose the noun form of the adjective 'wise'.
questions.explanation: The noun form of 'wise' is 'wisdom'. The others are adverb or comparative/superlative forms.

questions.question: Complete the lexical bundle: 'As a ___ of fact, I disagree with you.'
questions.explanation: 'As a matter of fact' is the fixed phrase. The other words do not form this bundle.

questions.question: 'To burn the midnight oil' means:
options: to work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: The idiom means to work or study till late at night; its meaning cannot be guessed from the individual words (opacity).

questions.question: 'The old river sang softly to the sleeping village.' Name the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: The river is given the human action of singing, which is personification. There is no 'like/as' (simile), no direct identity (metaphor) and no exaggeration.

questions.question: Which suffix is added to the adjective 'kind' to form the noun 'kindness'?
questions.explanation: '-ness' makes abstract nouns from adjectives (kind + ness). '-able', '-ify' and '-ous' form adjectives or verbs.

questions.question: In 'This suitcase is very light', the word 'light' means:
questions.explanation: Here 'light' describes weight. The other meanings of the polysemous word 'light' do not suit the context.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The ___ of the school addressed the students.
questions.explanation: 'Principal' (head of a school) is correct. 'Principle' means a rule or belief; 'principals' is plural and does not agree with 'the ... addressed'; 'principally' is an adverb.

questions.question: She always ___ attention to small details.
questions.explanation: 'Pay attention' is the standard collocation.

questions.question: Which of the following words can be used both as a noun and as a verb with the same spelling?
questions.explanation: 'Water' is a noun (a drink) and a verb (to water plants). 'Beautiful' and 'happy' are adjectives and 'quickly' is an adverb.

questions.question: 'A storm in a teacup' means:
options: a great fuss over a trivial matter
questions.explanation: The idiom means unnecessary excitement over a small matter.

questions.question: 'To cry wolf' means:
questions.explanation: From Aesop's fable, to cry wolf is to give a false warning so that people stop believing real ones. The other meanings are incorrect.

questions.question: 'All hands on deck!' uses 'hands' for sailors. This figure of speech is:
questions.explanation: Using a part ('hands') to stand for the whole (sailors) is synecdoche.

questions.question: Which of the following best sums up the central idea of the passage on libraries?
options: Libraries should be closed to save public money.
Printed books are always better than phones.
Libraries remain valuable and should be modernised, not closed.
Municipal bodies run libraries very efficiently.
questions.explanation: The author argues that libraries still serve many needs and calls for modernisation rather than closure. The other options contradict or misstate this.

questions.question: The word 'footfall' as used in the passage means:
questions.explanation: 'Footfall' in this context means the number of visitors coming to a place. The other meanings do not fit.

questions.question: The tone of the author is best described as:
questions.explanation: The writer argues earnestly and urges investment in libraries, so the tone is concerned and persuasive. There is no sarcasm, indifference or longing for the past.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a function of a modern library?
options: A place for students to prepare for examinations
A place for selling second-hand books
A place for retired people to read newspapers
A place where children discover stories
questions.explanation: The passage mentions exam preparation, newspaper reading and children discovering stories, but never selling books.

questions.question: 'But what is the price of a reading habit?' is an example of:
questions.explanation: The author does not expect an answer; the question is asked only to make a point, so it is rhetorical.

questions.question: The central theme of the poem is:
options: the joy of drinking cold water
the loss of a community meeting place and the memory it leaves behind
the poet's fear of deep water
a village festival at the well
questions.explanation: The poem contrasts the lively past of the well with its present silence while showing that its memory remains.

questions.question: 'Its water cool as the evening's first breeze' contains a:
questions.explanation: The comparison uses 'as' to compare water with a breeze, so it is a simile.

questions.question: The mood of the poem is mainly:
questions.explanation: The poet recalls the past with gentle regret, which is nostalgic and wistful. There is no anger, humour or celebration.

questions.question: Why does the poet mention the silent taps in the courtyards?
options: To show why people no longer go to the well
To complain about the cost of plumbing
To show the well water is dirty
questions.explanation: Taps at home mean villagers no longer need to walk to the well, which explains its abandonment. The poem does not mention cost or dirty water.

questions.question: The word 'frayed' in 'The rope is frayed' means:
options: worn and loose at the edges
questions.explanation: A frayed rope has its fibres worn and coming apart, suggesting long disuse.

questions.question: Why can most plants not use nitrogen directly from the air?
options: There is no nitrogen in the air.
They need sunlight to absorb it.
The two atoms are held by a bond too strong for them to break.
questions.explanation: The passage says atmospheric nitrogen has two atoms joined by a very strong bond that most plants cannot break. The air is nearly four-fifths nitrogen, so it is not absent.

questions.question: What does the plant give to the bacteria in return?
questions.explanation: The plant supplies the bacteria with sugars made in its leaves. Nitrogen is supplied by the bacteria to the plant.

questions.question: 'Symbiosis' as used in the passage means:
options: a relationship in which both organisms benefit
a relationship in which one organism harms the other
questions.explanation: The passage itself explains it as a partnership in which both organisms benefit.

questions.question: Which statement can be inferred from the passage?
options: Cereals fix nitrogen from the air.
Chemical fertilisers are cheap and harmless.
Rotating crops with pulses can lessen the need for chemical fertilisers.
Rhizobium lives in the leaves of pulses.
questions.explanation: Pulse crops enrich the soil with nitrogen, so less chemical fertiliser is needed. The passage says fertilisers are costly and polluting, and Rhizobium lives in root nodules.

questions.question: The tone of the passage is mainly:
questions.explanation: The passage explains a scientific process in a neutral, factual manner, so it is informative.

questions.question: What is the chief advantage of using learners' home languages as a resource in an English classroom?
questions.questionHi: अंग्रेज़ी कक्षा में बच्चों की घर की भाषाओं को संसाधन के रूप में प्रयोग करने का मुख्य लाभ क्या है?
options: It helps learners understand English by linking it to what they already know.
It replaces the teaching of English.
optionsHi: यह बच्चों के पहले से ज्ञात ज्ञान से जोड़कर अंग्रेज़ी समझने में मदद करता है।
यह अंग्रेज़ी शिक्षण की जगह ले लेता है।
यह शिक्षक की तैयारी कम करता है।
यह त्रुटियों को पूरी तरह रोक देता है।
questions.explanation: Home languages are a bridge: learners connect new English items to existing knowledge. They do not replace English, nor remove errors or the teacher's preparation.
questions.explanationHi: घर की भाषा एक पुल की तरह काम करती है, जिससे बच्चे नए अंग्रेज़ी शब्दों को अपने पुराने ज्ञान से जोड़ते हैं। यह अंग्रेज़ी की जगह नहीं लेती और न ही त्रुटियाँ या तैयारी खत्म करती है।

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of authentic material for teaching English?
questions.questionHi: अंग्रेज़ी पढ़ाने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा प्रामाणिक (authentic) सामग्री का उदाहरण है?
questions.explanation: Authentic materials are produced for real-life communication, not for teaching, such as advertisements, newspapers and notices. Graded readers and textbook exercises are written for learners.
questions.explanationHi: प्रामाणिक सामग्री वास्तविक जीवन में संप्रेषण के लिए बनी होती है, पढ़ाने के लिए नहीं, जैसे विज्ञापन, समाचार पत्र, सूचनाएँ। ग्रेडेड रीडर और पाठ्यपुस्तक के अभ्यास विद्यार्थियों के लिए लिखे जाते हैं।

questions.question: A learner's persistent, permanent errors that stop further progress in the second language are called:
questions.questionHi: दूसरी भाषा में सीखने वाले की ऐसी स्थायी त्रुटियाँ, जो आगे की प्रगति रोक देती हैं, कहलाती हैं:
questions.explanation: Fossilisation is the stage where incorrect forms become fixed in the learner's interlanguage.
questions.explanationHi: Fossilisation वह अवस्था है जिसमें गलत रूप learner की interlanguage में स्थायी हो जाते हैं।

questions.question: A learner occasionally says 'He go to school' but uses 'goes' correctly at other times and corrects himself when told. This is a:
questions.questionHi: एक विद्यार्थी कभी-कभी 'He go to school' कहता है, पर अन्य अवसरों पर 'goes' सही बोलता है और टोकने पर खुद सुधार लेता है। यह है:
questions.explanation: A mistake is a slip in performance; the learner knows the rule and can self-correct. Errors reflect gaps in knowledge and are systematic and not self-corrected.
questions.explanationHi: गलती (mistake) प्रदर्शन में चूक है; विद्यार्थी नियम जानता है और स्वयं सुधार लेता है। त्रुटि (error) ज्ञान की कमी दर्शाती है, वह लगातार होती है और स्वयं नहीं सुधरती।

questions.question: Which method teaches language through commands that learners respond to with physical actions?
questions.questionHi: कौन-सी विधि आदेशों पर शारीरिक क्रियाओं द्वारा प्रतिक्रिया करवाकर भाषा सिखाती है?
questions.explanation: James Asher's Total Physical Response links language with body movement in response to commands.
questions.explanationHi: जेम्स आशर की Total Physical Response में आदेशों के अनुसार शारीरिक क्रिया करके भाषा सीखी जाती है।

questions.question: 'Language is a habit formed through stimulus, response and reinforcement.' This view belongs to:
questions.questionHi: 'भाषा उद्दीपन, अनुक्रिया और पुनर्बलन से बनी आदत है।' यह मत किसका है?
questions.explanation: Skinner's behaviourist view treats language as learned behaviour shaped by reinforcement. Chomsky stresses an innate capacity; Vygotsky stresses social interaction; Piaget stresses cognitive development.
questions.explanationHi: स्किनर का व्यवहारवादी मत भाषा को पुनर्बलन से बना सीखा हुआ व्यवहार मानता है। चॉम्स्की जन्मजात क्षमता, वाइगोत्स्की सामाजिक अंतःक्रिया और पियाजे संज्ञानात्मक विकास पर बल देते हैं।

questions.question: A language laboratory is mainly useful for developing:
questions.questionHi: भाषा प्रयोगशाला मुख्यतः किसके विकास में उपयोगी है?
questions.explanation: Language labs use audio/recording equipment for listening and pronunciation practice.
questions.explanationHi: भाषा प्रयोगशाला में ऑडियो और रिकॉर्डिंग उपकरणों से सुनने व उच्चारण का अभ्यास होता है।

questions.question: The study of the smallest meaningful units of a language, such as 'un-', 'happy' and '-ness', is called:
questions.questionHi: भाषा की सबसे छोटी अर्थपूर्ण इकाइयों, जैसे 'un-', 'happy' और '-ness', के अध्ययन को कहते हैं:
questions.explanation: Morphology studies morphemes, the smallest meaningful units. Phonology studies sounds, syntax studies sentence structure and pragmatics studies meaning in context.
questions.explanationHi: रूपविज्ञान रूपिमों, यानी सबसे छोटी अर्थपूर्ण इकाइयों, का अध्ययन करता है। स्वनिमविज्ञान ध्वनियों, वाक्यविन्यास वाक्य संरचना और प्रयोगविज्ञान संदर्भ में अर्थ का अध्ययन करता है।

questions.question: The receptive skills of language are:
questions.questionHi: भाषा के ग्रहणशील (receptive) कौशल हैं:
questions.explanation: Listening and reading involve receiving language, so they are receptive. Speaking and writing are productive skills.
questions.explanationHi: सुनना और पढ़ना भाषा को ग्रहण करने के कौशल हैं, इसलिए ग्रहणशील हैं। बोलना और लिखना उत्पादक कौशल हैं।

questions.question: In first-language development, children first acquire language mainly through:
questions.questionHi: प्रथम भाषा के विकास में बच्चे सबसे पहले मुख्यतः किसके द्वारा भाषा अर्जित करते हैं?
questions.explanation: Children hear language around them long before they read or write, so listening comes first and speaking follows. Formal drills and writing come later.
questions.explanationHi: बच्चे पढ़ने-लिखने से बहुत पहले अपने आसपास की भाषा सुनते हैं, इसलिए सुनना पहले आता है और बोलना बाद में। औपचारिक अभ्यास और लेखन बाद में आते हैं।

questions.question: Which statement reflects the modern view of teaching grammar?
questions.questionHi: व्याकरण शिक्षण के बारे में आधुनिक दृष्टिकोण को कौन-सा कथन दर्शाता है?
options: Rules should be memorised in isolation.
Grammar should be taught in context to support communication.
Grammar can be taught only through translation.
optionsHi: नियमों को अलग से रटना चाहिए।
संप्रेषण में सहायता के लिए व्याकरण संदर्भ में पढ़ाना चाहिए।
व्याकरण को पूरी तरह छोड़ देना चाहिए।
व्याकरण केवल अनुवाद से पढ़ाया जा सकता है।
questions.explanation: The modern view treats grammar as a tool for communicating meaning, best learnt in meaningful context rather than by rote.
questions.explanationHi: आधुनिक दृष्टिकोण में व्याकरण अर्थ के संप्रेषण का साधन है, जिसे रटने की बजाय सार्थक संदर्भ में सीखना बेहतर है।

questions.question: Which method uses the mother tongue, translation of texts and teaching of rules, with emphasis on reading and writing?
questions.questionHi: कौन-सी विधि मातृभाषा, पाठों के अनुवाद और नियमों की शिक्षा का प्रयोग करती है तथा पढ़ने-लिखने पर बल देती है?
questions.explanation: The Grammar-Translation Method relies on translation and rules. The Direct Method avoids the mother tongue; Audio-lingual stresses oral drills; CLT stresses communication.
questions.explanationHi: व्याकरण-अनुवाद विधि अनुवाद और नियमों पर आधारित है। प्रत्यक्ष विधि मातृभाषा से बचती है, श्रव्य-भाषा विधि मौखिक अभ्यास और CLT संप्रेषण पर बल देती है।

questions.question: Which approach organises lessons around meaningful tasks such as planning a trip or solving a problem?
questions.questionHi: कौन-सा उपागम पाठों को सार्थक कार्यों, जैसे यात्रा की योजना बनाना या समस्या हल करना, के इर्द-गिर्द व्यवस्थित करता है?
questions.explanation: TBLT uses real tasks as the core of the lesson, and learners use language to complete them. The others focus on forms, rules or drills.
questions.explanationHi: TBLT में वास्तविक कार्य पाठ का केंद्र होते हैं और विद्यार्थी उन्हें पूरा करने के लिए भाषा का प्रयोग करते हैं। अन्य विधियाँ रूपों, नियमों या अभ्यास पर केंद्रित हैं।

questions.question: Krashen's 'Affective Filter' hypothesis says that:
questions.questionHi: क्रैशन की 'भावात्मक फ़िल्टर' परिकल्पना कहती है कि:
options: vocabulary is the most important element
anxiety and low motivation can block language input from being acquired
grammar is acquired in a fixed order
optionsHi: चिंता और कम प्रेरणा भाषा इनपुट के अर्जन को रोक सकती है
व्याकरण एक निश्चित क्रम में अर्जित होता है
questions.explanation: A high affective filter (fear, anxiety, low motivation) prevents input from reaching the acquisition system. Option 3 is the Natural Order hypothesis.
questions.explanationHi: ऊँचा भावात्मक फ़िल्टर (भय, चिंता, कम प्रेरणा) इनपुट को अर्जन प्रणाली तक पहुँचने से रोकता है। विकल्प 3 'प्राकृतिक क्रम' परिकल्पना है।

questions.question: In a classroom where learners speak different mother tongues, the teacher should:
questions.questionHi: जिस कक्षा में विद्यार्थी अलग-अलग मातृभाषाएँ बोलते हैं, वहाँ शिक्षक को चाहिए कि वह:
options: use only translation into one language
treat linguistic diversity as a resource and encourage learners to use all their languages
optionsHi: सभी घर की भाषाओं पर रोक लगा दे
केवल एक भाषा में अनुवाद का प्रयोग करे
भाषाई विविधता को संसाधन माने और विद्यार्थियों को अपनी सभी भाषाएँ प्रयोग करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करे
questions.explanation: Multilingualism is a classroom strength; using learners' languages helps understanding and inclusion. Banning languages or ignoring weaker learners harms learning.
questions.explanationHi: बहुभाषिकता कक्षा की ताकत है; विद्यार्थियों की भाषाओं के प्रयोग से समझ और समावेशन बढ़ता है। भाषाओं पर रोक लगाना या कमज़ोर विद्यार्थियों की उपेक्षा सीखने को नुकसान पहुँचाती है।

questions.question: Carl Rogers emphasised that a healthy self-concept develops through:
questions.questionHi: कार्ल रोजर्स के अनुसार स्वस्थ आत्म-संप्रत्यय किससे विकसित होता है?
questions.explanation: Rogers, a humanistic psychologist, stressed unconditional positive regard from significant others.
questions.explanationHi: मानवतावादी मनोवैज्ञानिक रोजर्स ने महत्वपूर्ण लोगों से बिना शर्त सकारात्मक सम्मान पर बल दिया।

questions.question: A dishonest person who accuses others of being dishonest is using the defence mechanism of:
questions.questionHi: एक बेईमान व्यक्ति दूसरों को बेईमान कहता है। वह कौन-सा रक्षा-तंत्र प्रयोग कर रहा है?
questions.explanation: Attributing one's own undesirable traits to others is projection.
questions.explanationHi: अपने अवांछित गुण दूसरों पर आरोपित करना projection है।

questions.question: In Gardner's theory of multiple intelligences, the ability to understand one's own feelings and goals is called:
questions.questionHi: गार्डनर के बहुबुद्धि सिद्धांत में अपनी भावनाओं और लक्ष्यों को समझने की क्षमता कहलाती है:
questions.explanation: Intrapersonal intelligence is self-understanding. Interpersonal intelligence is understanding other people.
questions.explanationHi: आत्म-वैयक्तिक (intrapersonal) बुद्धि स्वयं को समझने की क्षमता है, जबकि अंतर्वैयक्तिक (interpersonal) बुद्धि दूसरों को समझने की क्षमता है।

questions.question: Learning by observing and imitating the behaviour of others is the central idea of:
questions.questionHi: दूसरों के व्यवहार को देखकर और अनुकरण करके सीखना किसका केंद्रीय विचार है?
questions.explanation: Bandura showed that people learn by observation (modelling), as in the Bobo doll experiment. The other theories rely on conditioning or trial and error.
questions.explanationHi: बंडूरा ने दिखाया कि लोग अवलोकन (मॉडलिंग) से सीखते हैं, जैसा बोबो डॉल प्रयोग में देखा गया। अन्य सिद्धांत अनुबंधन या प्रयास-त्रुटि पर आधारित हैं।

questions.question: A child who obeys rules only to avoid punishment is at which level of Kohlberg's moral development?
questions.questionHi: जो बच्चा केवल दंड से बचने के लिए नियम मानता है, वह कोहलबर्ग के नैतिक विकास के किस स्तर पर है?
questions.explanation: Punishment-avoidance is Stage 1 of the pre-conventional level. Conventional morality is based on social approval and law; post-conventional on principles.
questions.explanationHi: दंड से बचना पूर्व-परंपरागत स्तर की पहली अवस्था है। परंपरागत नैतिकता सामाजिक स्वीकृति और कानून पर और उत्तर-परंपरागत सिद्धांतों पर आधारित होती है।

questions.question: A child who understands that the quantity of water stays the same when poured into a taller glass is in which Piagetian stage?
questions.questionHi: जो बच्चा समझता है कि पानी को लंबे गिलास में डालने पर उसकी मात्रा वही रहती है, वह पियाजे की किस अवस्था में है?
questions.explanation: Conservation is achieved in the concrete operational stage (about 7 to 11 years). Preoperational children (2 to 7) fail conservation tasks.
questions.explanationHi: संरक्षण की समझ मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था (लगभग 7 से 11 वर्ष) में आती है। पूर्व-संक्रियात्मक अवस्था (2 से 7 वर्ष) के बच्चे संरक्षण कार्यों में असफल रहते हैं।

questions.question: Giving the same test twice to the same group to check consistency of scores is the:
questions.questionHi: एक ही समूह को वही परीक्षण दो बार देकर अंकों की संगति जाँचना कहलाता है:
questions.explanation: The test-retest method estimates reliability by repeating the same test.
questions.explanationHi: Test-retest विधि में वही परीक्षण दोहराकर विश्वसनीयता ज्ञात की जाती है।

questions.question: When learners evaluate each other's work using given criteria, it is called:
questions.questionHi: जब विद्यार्थी दिए गए मापदंडों से एक-दूसरे के कार्य का मूल्यांकन करते हैं, तो वह है:
questions.explanation: Assessment by classmates is peer assessment.
questions.explanationHi: सहपाठियों द्वारा किया गया मूल्यांकन peer assessment है।

questions.question: A scoring guide that describes levels of performance for each criterion of a task is called a:
questions.questionHi: किसी कार्य के प्रत्येक मानदंड के लिए प्रदर्शन के स्तरों का वर्णन करने वाली अंकन-मार्गदर्शिका कहलाती है:
questions.explanation: A rubric lists criteria and performance levels, making scoring transparent. A blueprint plans a test's content and weightage.
questions.explanationHi: रूब्रिक में मानदंड और प्रदर्शन के स्तर दिए होते हैं, जिससे अंकन पारदर्शी होता है। ब्लूप्रिंट परीक्षा की विषयवस्तु और भारांक की योजना है।

questions.question: An open-book examination mainly tests:
questions.questionHi: खुली पुस्तक परीक्षा मुख्यतः किसकी जाँच करती है?
questions.explanation: Since material is available, questions focus on understanding and application.
questions.explanationHi: सामग्री उपलब्ध होने से प्रश्न समझ और अनुप्रयोग पर केंद्रित होते हैं।

questions.question: NCF 2005 recommends that learning should move away from:
questions.questionHi: NCF 2005 सुझाव देता है कि अधिगम को किससे दूर ले जाना चाहिए?
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 stresses meaningful, child-centred learning connected with life and discourages rote learning. The other three are encouraged.
questions.explanationHi: NCF 2005 जीवन से जुड़े, बाल-केंद्रित और अर्थपूर्ण अधिगम पर बल देता है और रटने को हतोत्साहित करता है। अन्य तीन को प्रोत्साहित किया गया है।

questions.question: NCF-SE 2023 organises school education into which stages?
questions.questionHi: NCF-SE 2023 स्कूली शिक्षा को किन चरणों में बाँटता है?
questions.explanation: Aligned with NEP 2020, the stages are Foundational (5), Preparatory (3), Middle (3) and Secondary (4). The 10+2 structure is the older one.
questions.explanationHi: NEP 2020 के अनुरूप चरण हैं: आधारभूत (5), तैयारी (3), मध्य (3) और माध्यमिक (4)। 10+2 पुरानी संरचना है।

questions.question: Learning objectives in a lesson plan should preferably be:
questions.questionHi: पाठ योजना में सीखने के उद्देश्य अधिमानतः कैसे होने चाहिए?
questions.explanation: Objectives stated in observable, measurable terms let the teacher check whether learning has taken place. Vague objectives cannot be assessed.
questions.explanationHi: अवलोकनीय और मापनीय उद्देश्य शिक्षक को जाँचने देते हैं कि सीखना हुआ या नहीं। अस्पष्ट उद्देश्यों का आकलन नहीं हो सकता।

questions.question: In a constructivist approach to teaching and learning, the teacher's main role is that of a:
questions.questionHi: रचनावादी कक्षा में शिक्षक मुख्यतः किस रूप में कार्य करता है?
questions.explanation: Constructivism holds that learners build knowledge themselves, so the teacher guides and facilitates. The other roles keep the learner passive.
questions.explanationHi: रचनावाद में विद्यार्थी स्वयं ज्ञान का निर्माण करते हैं, इसलिए शिक्षक मार्गदर्शन और सुगमन करता है। अन्य भूमिकाएँ विद्यार्थी को निष्क्रिय रखती हैं।

questions.question: A leader who involves the group in decision-making is called a:
questions.questionHi: जो नेता निर्णय लेने में समूह को शामिल करता है, वह कहलाता है:
questions.explanation: Democratic leadership encourages participation and shared decisions.
questions.explanationHi: लोकतांत्रिक नेतृत्व में भागीदारी और साझा निर्णय होते हैं।

questions.question: 'महेश' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद है:
questions.explanation: 'महा' के अंत का 'आ' और 'ईश' का 'ई' मिलकर गुण संधि से 'ए' बनता है, इसलिए महा + ईश = महेश।

questions.question: 'चक्रपाणि' (चक्र है हाथ में जिसके, अर्थात् विष्णु) में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: जब समस्त पद दोनों पदों से भिन्न किसी तीसरे (यहाँ विष्णु) का बोध कराए, तो बहुव्रीहि समास होता है। अन्य समासों में प्रधानता किसी पद की होती है।

questions.question: इनमें से कौन-सा शब्द 'कमल' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.explanation: पंकज, नीरज और अंबुज तीनों कमल के पर्यायवाची हैं, जबकि 'तरंग' का अर्थ लहर है।

questions.question: 'आदि' शब्द का विलोम है:
questions.explanation: 'आदि' का अर्थ शुरुआत है और उसका विलोम 'अंत' है। 'प्रारंभ' और 'आरंभ' उसके समानार्थी हैं, 'मध्य' बीच का भाग है।

questions.question: 'गुप्त' का विलोम शब्द चुनिए:
questions.explanation: 'गुप्त' (छिपा हुआ) का विलोम 'प्रकट' (सामने आया हुआ) है।

questions.question: Fill in the correct article: She is ___ honest woman.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so 'an' is used. 'A' is used before consonant sounds.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'diligent'.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means showing careful and persistent effort, i.e. hardworking. 'Lazy' and 'careless' are opposite in sense; 'clever' means intelligent.

questions.question: Change into passive voice: 'She is writing a letter.'
options: A letter was being written by her.
A letter is written by her.
A letter has been written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
questions.explanation: The present continuous active becomes 'is/am/are + being + past participle'. The other options use different tenses.

questions.question: A person who knows everything is called:
questions.explanation: Omniscient means all-knowing; omnipotent means all-powerful; omnipresent means present everywhere.

questions.question: Complete the proverb: 'Look before you ___.'
questions.explanation: The proverb is 'Look before you leap', meaning think before acting.

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 7, 9, 11, so the next difference is 13 and 35 + 13 = 48. (The terms are 2²-1, 3²-1, 4²-1, 5²-1, 6²-1, 7²-1.)

questions.question: If in a certain code CAT is written as ECV, how is DOG written in that code?
questions.questionHi: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में CAT को ECV लिखा जाता है, तो उसी भाषा में DOG को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved two places forward: C→E, A→C, T→V. So D→F, O→Q, G→I, giving FQI.
questions.explanationHi: प्रत्येक अक्षर दो स्थान आगे बढ़ाया गया है: C→E, A→C, T→V। अतः D→F, O→Q, G→I, यानी FQI।

questions.question: Looking at a boy, Rita said, 'He is the son of my mother's only brother.' The boy is Rita's:
questions.questionHi: एक लड़के को देखकर रीता ने कहा, 'वह मेरी माँ के इकलौते भाई का पुत्र है।' वह लड़का रीता का है:
questions.explanation: Rita's mother's brother is her maternal uncle (mama); his son is her cousin.
questions.explanationHi: रीता की माँ का भाई उसका मामा है; मामा का पुत्र उसका ममेरा भाई (cousin) हुआ।

questions.question: Find the next number: 4, 9, 19, 39, ?
questions.explanation: Each term = previous × 2 + 1, so 39 × 2 + 1 = 79.

questions.question: Pilot : Aeroplane :: Driver : ?
questions.questionHi: पायलट : हवाई जहाज़ :: चालक : ?
questions.explanation: A pilot operates an aeroplane, as a driver operates a car (person : vehicle driven).
questions.explanationHi: पायलट हवाई जहाज़ चलाता है, उसी प्रकार चालक कार चलाता है (व्यक्ति : चलाया जाने वाला वाहन)।

questions.question: Which component of a computer is known as its 'brain'?
questions.questionHi: कंप्यूटर का 'मस्तिष्क' किस भाग को कहा जाता है?
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) processes instructions and controls the computer. The monitor and mouse are output and input devices, and RAM is memory.
questions.explanationHi: CPU (केंद्रीय प्रसंस्करण इकाई) निर्देशों का प्रसंस्करण करती है और कंप्यूटर को नियंत्रित करती है। मॉनिटर आउटपुट, माउस इनपुट उपकरण और RAM मेमोरी है।

questions.question: Which one of these is a volatile type of memory?
questions.questionHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी वाष्पशील (volatile) मेमोरी है?
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents when power is switched off. ROM, hard disk and DVD retain data without power.
questions.explanationHi: बिजली बंद होने पर RAM का डेटा मिट जाता है। ROM, हार्ड डिस्क और DVD बिना बिजली के भी डेटा रखते हैं।

questions.question: FTP stands for:
questions.questionHi: FTP का पूर्ण रूप है:
questions.explanation: FTP is File Transfer Protocol, used to transfer files between computers over a network.
questions.explanationHi: FTP का अर्थ File Transfer Protocol है, जिससे नेटवर्क पर फ़ाइलें भेजी जाती हैं।

questions.question: In MS Excel, which key is used to edit the active cell?
questions.questionHi: MS Excel में सक्रिय सेल को संपादित करने के लिए कौन-सी कुंजी प्रयोग होती है?
questions.explanation: F2 puts the active cell in edit mode. F1 is Help and F12 is Save As.
questions.explanationHi: F2 से सक्रिय सेल edit mode में आता है। F1 Help और F12 Save As है।

questions.question: Which one of these is an open-source operating system?
questions.questionHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा ओपन-सोर्स ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम है?
questions.explanation: Linux's source code is freely available. Windows and MS-DOS are proprietary products of Microsoft.
questions.explanationHi: लिनक्स का सोर्स कोड सबके लिए उपलब्ध है। विंडोज़ और MS-DOS माइक्रोसॉफ्ट के स्वामित्व वाले उत्पाद हैं।

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees equality before the law?
questions.questionHi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद विधि के समक्ष समता की गारंटी देता है?
questions.explanation: Article 14 provides equality before law and equal protection of laws. Article 19 gives freedoms, Article 21 protects life and liberty and Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies.
questions.explanationHi: अनुच्छेद 14 विधि के समक्ष समता और विधियों के समान संरक्षण देता है। अनुच्छेद 19 स्वतंत्रताएँ, अनुच्छेद 21 जीवन व दैहिक स्वतंत्रता और अनुच्छेद 32 संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार है।

questions.question: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sunlight (UV-B) triggers synthesis of Vitamin D in the skin. Vitamin A, C and K are obtained mainly from food (K is also made by gut bacteria).
questions.questionHi: सूर्य के प्रकाश के संपर्क में आने पर मानव त्वचा में कौन-सा विटामिन बनता है?
questions.explanationHi: सूर्य के प्रकाश (UV-B) से त्वचा में विटामिन D बनता है। विटामिन A, C और K मुख्यतः भोजन से मिलते हैं (K आंत के बैक्टीरिया भी बनाते हैं)।

questions.question: The Chitrakote waterfall in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, is on which river?
questions.questionHi: छत्तीसगढ़ के बस्तर में स्थित चित्रकोट जलप्रपात किस नदी पर है?
questions.explanation: Chitrakote Falls, often called the 'Niagara of India', is on the Indravati river. Mahanadi, Shivnath and Hasdeo flow in other parts of the state.
questions.explanationHi: चित्रकोट जलप्रपात, जिसे 'भारत का नियाग्रा' भी कहा जाता है, इंद्रावती नदी पर स्थित है। महानदी, शिवनाथ और हसदेव राज्य के अन्य भागों में बहती हैं।

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the Red Fort in Delhi?
questions.questionHi: दिल्ली का लाल किला किस मुग़ल बादशाह ने बनवाया?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort (Lal Qila) at Shahjahanabad, Delhi, completed in 1648.
questions.explanationHi: शाहजहाँ ने शाहजहाँनाबाद (दिल्ली) में लाल किला बनवाया, जो 1648 में पूरा हुआ।

questions.question: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish-water lagoon of India, is located in:
questions.questionHi: भारत की सबसे बड़ी खारे पानी की लैगून चिल्का झील कहाँ स्थित है?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake lies on the coast of Odisha.
questions.explanationHi: चिल्का झील ओडिशा के तट पर स्थित है।
